Subject: RE: Fwd: RFI: data flow attestation and DPF evidence request

Jasmine — draft attached. Key points summarized below so we can iterate quickly. Attachment: DPF-Evidence-2028-03-07.pdf

High-level attestation (one paragraph):
Redwood Inference attests that customer input data is processed primarily in the region selected by the customer; where cross-border processing occurs Redwood relies on EU SCCs (or equivalent contractual safeguards) for transfers from the EEA to the US. For regulated customers requiring in-region processing we offer Private deployment options and Dedicated capacity that can be pinned to a region. Operational controls include network isolation, token-scoped KV cache controls, and key management integrations (KMS/HSM) with customer-managed key option.

Detailed points (bullets):
- Data flows: Ingest -> preprocessor -> inference runtime -> optional telemetry logging. Processing occurs in US, EU, and APAC cloud regions. Diagrams attached. (see dataflow-diagram.png)
- Legal basis: Standard SCCs adopted by Redwood; customers can request DPA annex with explicit transfer clauses. See redwood-dpa-annex-digest.docx for clause summaries.
- KMS: We use cloud KMS (GCP KMS / AWS KMS) for platform keys; HSM-backed customer KMS via BYOK available on Private deployments. Key custody options documented in attachment.
- Technical safeguards: prefix/KV cache TTLs, strict routing policies (region pinning, model variant fallbacks), and continuous batching safeguards to avoid cross-tenant leakage.
- Retention: Customer-supplied payloads are retained per contracted retention; default ephemeral token caches (minutes to hours depending on config). We provide deletion APIs and audit logs for deletion events.
- Evidence: SOC2 report references and internal control mapping included in PDF (redacted where required).

Open items for SentinelBridge:
1) Do they need processor-subprocessor export lists (we can provide a subprocessor registry extract)?
2) Will they accept SCCs or require additional contractual language?
3) Any specific retention baseline they expect (30/90/365 days)?

I can tighten wording into an attestation memo for Samir once we agree on the open items.

-Karthik
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference
attachments: DPF-Evidence-2028-03-07.pdf, dataflow-diagram.png, redwood-dpa-annex-digest.docx

Hi Samir / Anna / LegalOps team,

Thanks for the list — attached is our attestation and supporting artifacts for your compliance review next week. Summary highlights:

- Attestation: Redwood Inference attests that we process customer-provided data in the region selected by the customer and rely on standard EU SCCs for any EEA->US transfers. Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated capacity options exist for customers needing in-region-only processing. (See attached PDF, first page.)
- Data flows: See attached diagram (dataflow-diagram.png) showing ingest, inference runtime, optional telemetry, and storage tiers. Processing regions: US (primary), EU (Frankfurt), APAC (Singapore).
- KMS & keys: We support cloud KMS (GCP/AWS) and customer-managed BYOK with HSM backing for Private deployments. Onboarding SLA for BYOK is typically 5 business days after key exchange.
- Safeguards: KV/prefix cache TTLs are configurable and default to short durations; routing policies allow region pinning and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity-constrained. Audit logs capture routing decisions and deletion events; extracts are available upon request with retention of 1 year by default (longer by contract).
- Retention and training: Customer input is not used for model training by default. If a customer elects training usage, that will be explicitly reflected in contract terms and the customer's opt-in settings.

Attachments included: DPF-Evidence-2028-03-07.pdf (attestation + control mapping), dataflow-diagram.png, redwood-dpa-annex-digest.docx (clause summaries). Also shared a Drive folder with redacted SOC2 references and subprocessor registry: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SentinelBridgeRFI

Next steps: please confirm whether SCCs are acceptable or if you need supplemental language for the DPA annex. We're happy to provide a redlined DPA annex if helpful — I can coordinate with LegalOps on our side.

If helpful, Karthik and Soojin can join a 30-minute call on Fri 3/9 to walk through technical controls.
